subject: Request for processing ledger extract and subprocessor change log for DPIA
body:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobaltbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: security.team@cobaltbank.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2027 09:23:00 -0400
Subject: Request: processing ledger extract + subprocessor change log for DPIA

Hi Jonas,

As part of our DPIA refresh next week I need an extract of Redwood's processing ledger (Article 30) covering Jan 1, 2025 through present, and a subprocessor change log that shows all subprocessor additions/terminations for Q1–Q2 2027. Our legal team also wants any documentation you can share about transfer destinations (third countries) and whether any subprocessors export data outside the EU/US.

Deliverables we need by Friday 16 July if possible:
- CSV export of the Article 30 ledger (fields: processing purpose, category of data subjects, category of personal data, recipients, transfers, retention period, technical/organizational measures)
- Subprocessor change log (CSV) with timestamps and contract version references
- Short narrative (1 page) describing how Redwood records transfers and what safeguards are in place (SCCs, binding corporate rules, etc.)

If any of these items require an NDA or escalation, let me know. Happy to accept redacted samples for review.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Privacy Operations
Cobalt Bank
elena.ruiz@cobaltbank.com

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobaltbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2027 11:05:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: processing ledger extract + subprocessor change log for DPIA

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're able to pull the ledger and change log but a couple quick clarifying Qs so we scope exactly what you need: 

1) For the Article 30 export, do you need every customer-facing entry (we can include customer IDs) or a supplier-wide ledger (redacted customer identifiers)?
2) For transfers: do you want flagging of destination countries only, or the raw transfer destination endpoints (e.g., AWS regions, partner endpoints)?
3) For the subprocessor change log, should we include contract revision IDs (internal) or only the public-facing effective dates?

I'm looping in Mina from Privacy Ops and Karthik from Compliance so they can prepare a packaged export and narrative. We'll aim to get a redacted sample to you tomorrow for confirmation.

Regards,
Jonas
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobaltbank.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 10:37:04 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: processing ledger extract + subprocessor change log for DPIA

Hi Elena — attaching a redacted sample and notes. Quick summary of what I attached and limitations: 

Attachments (sample):
- processing-ledger-2027-07.csv (CSV, redacted customer IDs; retains processing purpose, data categories, recipients, transfers, retention)
- subprocessor-change-log-2027Q2.csv (CSV, lists added/removed subprocessors with timestamps; contract reference column shows which DPA amendment covered the change)
- redwood-dpia-guidance.pdf (PDF, short narrative on transfer safeguards and retention governance)

Notes: 
- We redact direct customer identifiers by default; if you need full customer IDs we require a signed Data Access Addendum (small formality for audit exports).
- Transfer destinations include region tags and, where relevant, a destination country column for clarity. We do not include low-level endpoint URLs in this export; we can provide them under a controlled access request.
- The change log shows the effective timestamp and the contract amendment ID; internal ticket links are redacted.

If this sample meets your needs we can produce the full ledger CSV. Let me know if you want the export to include historical snapshots (we can include a 'version' column per row).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Privacy Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
[attachment: processing-ledger-2027-07.csv (csv)]
[attachment: subprocessor-change-log-2027Q2.csv (csv)]
[attachment: redwood-dpia-guidance.pdf (pdf)]

---

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobaltbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 12:00:20 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: processing ledger extract + subprocessor change log for DPIA

Mina — thanks, that sample looks good. Two follow-ups: 
1) Please ensure the full change log includes subprocessors that were active at any point in Q1 and Q2 (not just additions/removals). Our DPIA reviewers want an inclusive list for the quarter.
2) Can you add a short narrative (bullet points) summarizing which subprocessors have cross-border processing and whether SCCs or equivalent safeguards apply to those flows? A one-paragraph blurb for each named processor would be ideal.

If an access addendum is needed for full customer IDs we can route it through legal — please send the template.

Thanks,
Elena

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cobaltbank.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 16:12:08 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: processing ledger extract + subprocessor change log for DPIA

Elena — following up with the full package. Highlights below and attached files (for ease I’ve included filenames):

- Full ledger CSV: processing-ledger-2027-07.csv — includes a 'historical_activity' flag for rows modified during Q1–Q2 2027. Customer IDs are redacted; if you confirm the Data Access Addendum we will release full IDs.
- Subprocessor compilation: subprocessor-change-log-2027Q2.csv — includes an "active_during_quarter" column that flags processors active in Q1 and/or Q2. We included contract revision ID and whether standard contractual clauses are in place.
- Narrative: the attached PDF (redwood-dpia-guidance.pdf) contains a 1-page summary per requested processor describing cross-border status and safeguards.

Short narrative excerpt (for reviewers):
- Most data transfers for production inference occur to cloud regions (AWS GCP) listed by region tag. Transfers to third countries are covered by SCCs (where applicable) and contractual commitments in our DPA.
- Where subprocessors perform maintenance or analytics outside the EEA, we have either SCCs or documented legal basis with additional technical controls (encryption at rest, restricted access).
- We can provide a formal attestation letter for auditors on request (requires a DPIA support addendum).

Next steps: if you want full customer identifiers, please sign the Data Access Addendum (I attached a draft in the Drive link below). If auditors need live access to ledger views we can set up a time-limited access window.

Drive link (packaged export): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcExample

If anything else is needed for your DPIA packet, ping me and I'll prioritize.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
